title: [gpu] Pin the validated ragged all-to-all PJRT wheel
body:
Pin the ARM64 CUDA 13 PJRT wheel to XLA `708c3a4ec79c`, which uses 32 thread blocks of 512 threads, sender-relative peer ordering, and eight-load copy batches for the opt-in ragged all-to-all device kernel. The stock JAX, jaxlib, and CUDA plugin generation remains 0.11.1.

[Three matched EP64/GB200 pairs](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/407) measured 2.766% higher training throughput for the 32 × 256 geometry, peer ordering, and copy changes versus the previous 152 × 128 kernel. A separate three-pair comparison measured 0.699% higher throughput for 512 versus 256 threads at fixed 32 blocks, peer ordering, and copy batches. Each comparison includes all 60 scored steps per run after 20 fixed warmup steps, including latency spikes; these estimates come from different run windows and should not be added. They do not establish reduced spike frequency or long-run convergence.

The [promoted wheel](https://github.com/marin-community/xla/releases/tag/marin-xla-pjrt-20260915-708c3a4ec79c) was built on Iris and passed two-device GB200 output correctness and device-kernel engagement checks. Its immutable release includes the source revisions, wheel hash, and validation record. The safe CPU suite passed 1,858 tests; all 11 Tasktrove failures reproduced on unchanged `main`.


The hero trigger now names the relaunch that deploys this wheel together with the PDL-off QuACK launchers from #9183: run id `hero-nopdl-step108k`, initialized from `hero-mix-996f4891-step108k`'s hourly checkpoint `step-108778`, whose metadata is marked non-temporary so the old run's later saves keep it. The old run trains 200 steps past that checkpoint as the paired control for the trial window (#8870).
